predecessors.name: Byzantine Empire
predecessors.text: the Taurus country around Sis and Vahka, where Ruben 'revolted against Byzantium in 1080'; the page gives no boundary, so the first Cliopatria shape stands for it

predecessors.name: Bagratid Armenia
predecessors.text: Ruben was 'linked to Gagik II' of Bagratid Armenia; the infobox lists it as a predecessor

successors.name: Mamluk Sultanate
successors.text: Adana and Tarsus (1359) and 'the remaining areas of Cilicia' (1375), with Sis falling on 13 April 1375

successors.name: Ramadanid Emirate
successors.text: the Ramadanid Turkmen emirate in Cilicia, authorised by the Mamluks; Adana its centre

successors.name: Kingdom of Cyprus
successors.text: title only: the Armenian crown passed to James I of Cyprus in 1396

ledger.x: c. 1080: Ruben founds the Armenian princedom of Cilicia. 'Ruben, linked to Gagik II, revolted against Byzantium in 1080 and the foundations of the independent Armenian princedom of Cilicia were laid'; infobox 'Founded: c. 1080 as the Rubenid principality'. The page gives no boundary.
c. 1100: Thoros I moves the capital from Tarsus to Sis. The page says he succeeded 'around 1100' and moved the capital; the infobox has Tarsus to 1198.
1129-1137: Levon I integrates the coastal cities.
1137: John II conquers Cilicia.
After 1141: Thoros, freed from Constantinople, takes Vahka.
1144/1145: Thoros II becomes lord of Armenian Cilicia.
1151: Thoros II takes Mamistra and Tel Hamdoun from the Byzantines.
Page silent: no page opened dates the recovery of Tarsus, Adana and Anazarbus (Adana is named only as a hunting ground); Cliopatria draws them from 1147, the page's Mamistra from 1151.
1191: Leo captures Bagras from Saladin's hands.
Page silent on the year: Leo 'conquered Isauria and came as far as [Iconium]' and 'doubled its Mediterranean coast', all after 1187 and undated; the year is Cliopatria's.
6 January 1198: Leo is crowned king, and the principality becomes a kingdom.
c. 1204: Leo seizes Antiochene fortresses in the Amanus after Renoart's rebellion; 'His 1205 siege of Trapessac (25 December) failed'. The page gives 'around 1204' and no list of places.
14 February 1216: Leo enters Antioch.
1219: Bohemond IV regains Antioch.
14 June 1226: the Hethumids join the Rubenids on the throne.
Page silent on the year: Karaman Bey's conquests of the 1240s 'were mainly at the expense of Lesser Armenia' (Karamanids page, with Larende and Ermenek given c.
Page silent on the year: 'Marash and Behesni were recovered in the 1250s'; Cliopatria's 1260 shape reaches 38.2 E.

c. 1260: Mut and Ermenek pass to the Karamanids. 'c. 1260: Kilij Arslan IV gave Karaman Bey Larende and Ermenek'; the infobox dates the Battle of Mut to 1260. The page says the Seljuk gave the lands, so the Armenian share is the reading of the earlier conquests.
1342: Guy de Lusignan is anointed as Constantine II after Levon IV's assassination in 1341; the Hethumids give way to the Lusignans within the same state.
1359: the Mamluks take Adana and Tarsus.
13 April 1375: Sis falls to the Mamluks; Gaban follows.
13 April 1375: the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia ends.

wars.name: Byzantine conquest of Cilicia (John II Komnenos)
wars.outcome: John II took most cities of the plains and the principality; Leo, Roupen and Thoros were captured, and Cilicia stayed Byzantine for eight years.

wars.name: Thoros II's wars with Byzantium and Antioch
wars.outcome: Thoros took Mamistra and Tel Hamdoun in 1151, faced Masud at Anazarbus in 1154 and gave up Berdus to Kilij Arslan in 1157; in 1158 he paid homage to Manuel I in a treaty.

wars.name: Leo I's Bagras war
wars.outcome: Leo captured and kept Bagras in 1191; the 1192 peace, brokered by Henry II of Champagne, had Leo and Bohemond renounce suzerainty claims and left Bagras with Leo.

wars.name: War of the Antiochene Succession
wars.outcome: Leo seized Amanus fortresses around 1204, held Antioch from 14 February 1216 for Raymond-Roupen and lost it to Bohemond IV in 1219; the war 'came to a rather unspectacular end' with Leo's death in May 1219.

wars.name: Rum conquests of Armenian forts and the vassalage of 1225
wars.outcome: Kaykaus I captured Armenian forts north of the Taurus while Leo was in Antioch; Kayqubad I's Cilicia campaign of 1225 'reduced the kingdom of Cilician Armenia to a vassal state'.

wars.name: Mongol alliance and the war with Rum (1244-1259)
wars.outcome: Hethum I submitted to the Mongols after Köse Dağ (1244), sent Sempad to Karakorum in 1247, was attacked by Rum in 1245, visited Möngke in 1253-1256 and fought beside Hulagu in 1259-1260; Marash and Behesni were recovered in the 1250s.

wars.name: Mamluk invasions of Cilicia
wars.outcome: Mari (1266): Thoros killed, Leo captured, Sis sacked and burnt, Hethum ransomed his son by conceding unnamed territory; Tarsus taken in 1275; ten-year truce of 1285 with ceded fortresses and a tribute of one million dirhams a year; Hromgla sacked in 1292…

wars.name: Mamluk conquest of the Cilician plain
wars.outcome: A Mamluk invasion in 1343-1344; in 1359 the Mamluk army took Adana and Tarsus; the Ramadanid Turkmen emirate was authorised to administer Cilicia from 1352.

wars.name: Fall of Sis
wars.outcome: Sis fell on 13 April 1375 and Gaban followed; the Mamluks took the remaining areas of Cilicia.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey lines are given by any page; the principality and kingdom were chains of castles and cities in the Taurus and on the Cilician plain, and their outline is approximate throughout.
